_strings.@@fb00d460968b: Treaty conformity — LA conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from LA income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the LA return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: LA's resident return (IT-540) starts from Federal Adjusted Gross Income: Line 7 is "FEDERAL ADJUSTED GROSS INCOME" and the 2024 instructions say "Line 7 – Enter the amount of your Federal Adjusted Gross Income (Federal AGI). This amount is taken from Federal Form 1040 or 1040-SR, Line 11. If your Federal AGI is less than zero, enter 0." Federally treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal AGI and therefore flows through. The only "additions" to federal AGI are on Schedule E, Lines 2A-2D: (2A) interest and dividend income from other states and their political subdivisions, (2B) recapture of START contributions, (2C) recapture of START K12 contributions, and (2D) add back of pass-through entity loss. There is NO add-back of tax-treaty-exempt income anywhere on the IT-540 form, Schedule E, or in the instructions (the word "treaty" appears zero times in both the 2024 IT-540 form PDF and the 2024 IT-540 instructions PDF). Because LA starts from federal AGI and has no treaty addback, treaty-exempt income is not re-taxed -> conforms.
_strings.@@fb671516727e: Louisiana Nonrefundable Child Care Credit (federal AGI greater than $25,000) — Louisiana residents with federal adjusted gross income greater than $25,000 who incurred qualifying child and dependent care expenses (IRC Section 21) in Louisiana and claimed a federal child care credit. Unused credit may be carried forward up to five years (for 2024, carryforwards from 2019 through 2023 may be applied; 2018 amounts have expired). Authorized by R.S. 47:297.4.

Pack notes: Base guidance: Supply 2024 Form IT-540, Line 9: 'Subtract Line 8D from Line 7. If less than zero, enter zero 0' (YOUR LOUISIANA TAX TABLE INCOME). Line 7 is Federal Adjusted Gross Income (Federal Form 1040/1040-SR, Line 11; if less than zero enter 0; if you have Louisiana additions/exempt income, Line 7 comes from Louisiana Schedule E, Line 5 instead). Line 8D, 'EXCESS FEDERAL ITEMIZED DEDUCTIONS,' applies only to federal itemizers and equals Line 8B (federal itemized deduction for medical and dental expenses, federal Schedule A Line 4) minus Line 8C (2024 federal standard deduction: $14,600 statuses 1/3, $29,200 statuses 2/5, $21,900 status 4), floor zero. IMPORTANT: supply Line 9 UNREDUCED - do NOT subtract Louisiana's $4,500/$9,000 combined personal exemption-standard deduction yourself; it is encoded in the zero-rate bottom bracket shipped here (standard_deduction is null for that reason). Adjudication note (two-pass): base is federal_agi — IT-540 Line 7 is federal adjusted gross income and Line 9 tax table income derives from it (see base-quirk note); supply Line 9. exemptions_count must be 0: the primary personal exemptions are BUILT INTO the zero-rate floor ($4,500 single/MFS; $9,000 MFJ/QSS and Head of Household per the printed 2024 table headers), never subtracted separately. 2024 rates, boundaries, and floors verified identical to 2023 in both the printed tax tables and the IT-540B Tax Computation Worksheet. 2024 IS THE LAST GRADUATED YEAR: Louisiana adopted a FLAT 3% individual income tax effective for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2025 (2024 Third Extraordinary Session). The 2025 IT-540 documents print the flat structure — never source 2024 figures from them, and never use this 2024 pack for 2025. Table mandate below $51,000 ($101,000 for MFJ/QSS): IT-540 Line 10 requires taking the tax from the printed 2024 Louisiana Tax Table for your filing status and Line 6F exemption count - bracket math may differ by a few dollars within table bands (the printed cells equal the IT-540B worksheet math evaluated at the midpoint of each $250 income band in every cell sampled — e.g., Single 1-exemption $12,500-$12,750 cell prints 152 = 1.85% x 8,000 + 3.5% x 125 at midpoint 12,625 rounded; MFJ 2-exemption $89,750-$90,000 cell prints 2,567 = 296 + 3.5% x 64,875 at midpoint 89,875 rounded); the filed form must use the table. Above the table cap, the table itself prescribes 'Plus 4.25% of Tax Table Income in Excess of $51,000' ($101,000 MFJ/QSS) added to the last printed row, which was computed at that band's midpoint ($50,875/$100,875) - the official method therefore comes out about $5 below exact bracket math. Qualifying Surviving Spouse (filing status 5) shares the Married Filing Jointly tax table, brackets, and $9,000 combined deduction - the engine's QSS -> married_filing_jointly mapping is exact. Head of Household shares the Single/MFS bracket boundaries ($12,500/$50,000) but gets the $9,000 combined personal exemption-standard deduction ($4,500 more than Single) - hence its different zero-rate floor. The zero-rate floor covers only the base exemption count (one exemption for Single/MFS/HOH; two for MFJ/QSS - the MFJ/QSS table has no one-exemption column, and Line 6 requires the same exemptions as your federal return except for the dependent-on-another's-return, 65-or-over, and blind cases). Every additional Line 6F exemption ($1,000 each - dependents, 65-or-over boxes, blind boxes) is handled per the shipped 'dependent'/'age_65'/'blind' entries and their noted engine divergence. Louisiana credits are NOT modeled by this op and come off after Line 10: Nonrefundable Priority 1 credits (Schedule C) on Line 11; refundable child care credit (federal AGI <= $25,000, worksheet decimal .35-.30 x 50%), refundable school readiness credit (star-rated 200%/150%/100%/50%), and the Louisiana Earned Income Credit (5% of the federal EIC) on Lines 13-15; other refundable Priority 2/4 credits (Schedules F and I) and nonrefundable Priority 3 credits including the nonrefundable child care credit (Schedule J, 30%/10% with the $25 cap over $60,000 AGI) on Lines 16/20/25. Base quirk (affects the figure you supply, not this computation): Louisiana's only deduction between federal AGI and tax table income is Line 8D 'EXCESS FEDERAL ITEMIZED DEDUCTIONS' = federal itemized MEDICAL AND DENTAL deduction (Schedule A Line 4) minus the 2024 federal standard deduction ($14,600/$29,200/$21,900), floor zero, for federal itemizers only - non-itemizers skip Lines 8A-8D. Consumer Use Tax (Line 22A boxes) and the Electric/Hybrid Vehicle Road Usage Fee (Line 22B) are separate amounts added on the 2024 return after the income tax - NOT modeled.
